claim: Human herpesviruses 6A and 6B (HHV-6A/6B) share approximately 90% sequence identity.
source: Human herpesviruses 6A and 6B (HHV-6A/6B; species Human betaherpesvirus 6A and Human betaherpesvirus 6B) are closely related viruses, sharing approximately 90% sequence identity (Ablashi et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Ablashi et al., 2014.

claim: HHV-6A/6B genomes comprise a unique region (U) of approximately 140 kb flanked on each side by a direct repeat (DR) of approximately 8 kb.
source: Their genomes comprise a unique region (U) of approximately 140 kb flanked on each side by a direct repeat (DR) of approximately 8 kb (DRL on the left and DRR on the right).
evidence: The claim is supported by established knowledge about HHV-6A/6B genome structure.

claim: T1 at one end of DR consists of 1–8 kb of telomere (TTAGGG) and degenerate telomere-like repeats.
source: T1 at one end of DR consists of 1–8 kb of telomere (TTAGGG) and degenerate telomere-like repeats (Huang et al., 2014; Lindquester and Pellett, 1991; Zhang et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Huang et al., 2014; Lindquester and Pellett, 1991; Zhang et al., 2017.

claim: T2 at the other end of DR is much shorter and contains only (TTAGGG) repeats.
source: T2 at the other end of DR is much shorter and contains only (TTAGGG) repeats (Achour et al., 2009; Zhang et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Achour et al., 2009; Zhang et al., 2017.

claim: HHV-6A/6B have the capacity to integrate into human telomeres, most likely through a homology-dependent recombination mechanism facilitated by the perfect telomere repeats in T2.
source: HHV-6A/6B have the capacity to integrate into human telomeres, most likely through a homology-dependent recombination mechanism facilitated by the perfect telomere repeats in T2 (Arbuckle et al., 2010; Wallaschek et al., 2016b).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Arbuckle et al., 2010; Wallaschek et al., 2016b.

claim: HHV-6A/6B infect over 90% of the global population in early childhood.
source: HHV-6A/6B infect over 90% of the global population in early childhood; this usually manifests with mild symptoms but nevertheless often requires medical attention (Asano et al., 1994; Hall et al., 1994; Kondo et al., 1993; Ward and Gray, 1994; Zerr et al., 2005).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Asano et al., 1994; Hall et al., 1994; Kondo et al., 1993; Ward and Gray, 1994; Zerr et al., 2005.

claim: Reactivation of free virus acquired in the community (acqHHV-6A/6B) has been shown to cause viral encephalitis, drug-induced hypersensitivity syndrome/drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DIHS/DRESS), and acute graft-versus-host disease (aGVHD).
source: Reactivation of free virus acquired in the community (acqHHV-6A/6B) has been shown to cause viral encephalitis, drug-induced hypersensitivity syndrome/drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DIHS/DRESS), and acute graft-versus-host disease (aGVHD) (Aihara et al., 2003; Eshki et al., 2009; Pritchett et al., 2012; Prusty, 2018; Yao et al., 2010; Yoshikawa et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Aihara et al., 2003; Eshki et al., 2009; Pritchett et al., 2012; Prusty, 2018; Yao et al., 2010; Yoshikawa et al., 2006.

claim: HHV-6A infection has been associated with multiple sclerosis and other chronic neurological conditions.
source: In addition, HHV-6A infection has been associated with multiple sclerosis and other chronic neurological conditions (Yao et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Yao et al., 2010.

claim: Approximately 1% of the population carries inherited chromosomally integrated HHV-6A/6B (iciHHV-6A/6B), usually with a full-length copy of the viral genome in every cell.
source: As a result of historical germline integrations into telomeres, approximately 1% of the population carries inherited chromosomally integrated HHV-6A/6B (iciHHV-6A/6B), usually with a full-length copy of the viral genome in every cell (Arbuckle et al., 2010; Daibata et al., 1999; Huang et al., 2014; Leong et al., 2007; Morris et al., 1999; Tanaka-Taya et al., 2004).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Arbuckle et al., 2010; Daibata et al., 1999; Huang et al., 2014; Leong et al., 2007; Morris et al., 1999; Tanaka-Taya et al., 2004.

claim: iciHHV-6B is commonly found integrated into the telomere on the short arm of chromosome 17 (17p) in populations of European descent.
source: For example, iciHHV-6B is commonly found integrated into the telomere on the short arm of chromosome 17 (17p) in populations of European descent and iciHHV-6A is commonly found in the long arm of chromosome 22 (22q) in Japan.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about iciHHV-6B integration patterns.

claim: iciHHV-6A is commonly found in the long arm of chromosome 22 (22q) in Japan.
source: For example, iciHHV-6B is commonly found integrated into the telomere on the short arm of chromosome 17 (17p) in populations of European descent and iciHHV-6A is commonly found in the long arm of chromosome 22 (22q) in Japan.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about iciHHV-6A integration patterns.

claim: The presence of a large viral genome within a telomere has been shown to cause localized instability that may influence telomere DNA damage signaling and function.
source: Similarly, the presence of a large viral genome within a telomere has been shown to cause localized instability that may influence telomere DNA damage signaling and function (Huang et al., 2014; Wood and Royle, 2017; Zhang et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Huang et al., 2014; Wood and Royle, 2017; Zhang et al., 2016.

claim: Recent studies have indicated an association between iciHHV-6A/6B and angina pectoris.
source: Recent studies have also indicated an association between iciHHV-6A/6B and angina pectoris (Gravel et al., 2015); unexplained infertility (Miura et al., 2020); an increased risk of aGVHD following hematopoietic stem cell transplantation when either the donor or recipient has iciHHV-6A/6B (Hill et al., 2017; Weschke et al., 2020); complications following solid organ transplantation when there was iciHHV-6A/6B donor/recipient mismatch (Bonnafous et al., 2018; Bonnafous et al., 2020; Petit et al., 2020); and possibly an increased risk of pre-eclampsia (Gaccioli et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Gravel et al., 2015.

claim: Recent studies have indicated an association between iciHHV-6A/6B and unexplained infertility.
source: Recent studies have also indicated an association between iciHHV-6A/6B and angina pectoris (Gravel et al., 2015); unexplained infertility (Miura et al., 2020); an increased risk of aGVHD following hematopoietic stem cell transplantation when either the donor or recipient has iciHHV-6A/6B (Hill et al., 2017; Weschke et al., 2020); complications following solid organ transplantation when there was iciHHV-6A/6B donor/recipient mismatch (Bonnafous et al., 2018; Bonnafous et al., 2020; Petit et al., 2020); and possibly an increased risk of pre-eclampsia (Gaccioli et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Miura et al., 2020.

claim: Recent studies have indicated an increased risk of aGVHD following hematopoietic stem cell transplantation when either the donor or recipient has iciHHV-6A/6B.
source: Recent studies have also indicated an association between iciHHV-6A/6B and angina pectoris (Gravel et al., 2015); unexplained infertility (Miura et al., 2020); an increased risk of aGVHD following hematopoietic stem cell transplantation when either the donor or recipient has iciHHV-6A/6B (Hill et al., 2017; Weschke et al., 2020); complications following solid organ transplantation when there was iciHHV-6A/6B donor/recipient mismatch (Bonnafous et al., 2018; Bonnafous et al., 2020; Petit et al., 2020); and possibly an increased risk of pre-eclampsia (Gaccioli et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Hill et al., 2017; Weschke et al., 2020.

claim: Recent studies have indicated complications following solid organ transplantation when there was iciHHV-6A/6B donor/recipient mismatch.
source: Recent studies have also indicated an association between iciHHV-6A/6B and angina pectoris (Gravel et al., 2015); unexplained infertility (Miura et al., 2020); an increased risk of aGVHD following hematopoietic stem cell transplantation when either the donor or recipient has iciHHV-6A/6B (Hill et al., 2017; Weschke et al., 2020); complications following solid organ transplantation when there was iciHHV-6A/6B donor/recipient mismatch (Bonnafous et al., 2018; Bonnafous et al., 2020; Petit et al., 2020); and possibly an increased risk of pre-eclampsia (Gaccioli et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Bonnafous et al., 2018; Bonnafous et al., 2020; Petit et al., 2020.

claim: Recent studies have indicated possibly an increased risk of pre-eclampsia associated with iciHHV-6A/6B.
source: Recent studies have also indicated an association between iciHHV-6A/6B and angina pectoris (Gravel et al., 2015); unexplained infertility (Miura et al., 2020); an increased risk of aGVHD following hematopoietic stem cell transplantation when either the donor or recipient has iciHHV-6A/6B (Hill et al., 2017; Weschke et al., 2020); complications following solid organ transplantation when there was iciHHV-6A/6B donor/recipient mismatch (Bonnafous et al., 2018; Bonnafous et al., 2020; Petit et al., 2020); and possibly an increased risk of pre-eclampsia (Gaccioli et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Gaccioli et al., 2020.

claim: There is increasing evidence that iciHHV-6A/6B genomes can reactivate fully.
source: There is increasing evidence that iciHHV-6A/6B genomes can reactivate fully (Endo et al., 2014) and then be transmitted as acqHHV-6A/6B (Gravel et al., 2013; Hall et al., 2010), but the chain of events leading to reactivation is unknown.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Endo et al., 2014.

claim: iciHHV-6A/6B can be transmitted as acqHHV-6A/6B.
source: There is increasing evidence that iciHHV-6A/6B genomes can reactivate fully (Endo et al., 2014) and then be transmitted as acqHHV-6A/6B (Gravel et al., 2013; Hall et al., 2010), but the chain of events leading to reactivation is unknown.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Gravel et al., 2013; Hall et al., 2010.

claim: Telomeres are terminated by a single-stranded 3′ overhang that can strand-invade into the upstream double-stranded telomeric DNA to form a telomere loop (t-loop).
source: Telomeres are terminated by a single-stranded 3′ overhang that can strand-invade into the upstream double-stranded telomeric DNA to form a telomere loop (t-loop) (Doksani et al., 2013; Griffith et al., 1999; Wang et al., 2004).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Doksani et al., 2013; Griffith et al., 1999; Wang et al., 2004.

claim: The t-loop secondary structure is stabilized by TRF2, a component of the Shelterin complex that binds to double-stranded telomere repeats.
source: This secondary structure is stabilized by TRF2, a component of the Shelterin complex that binds to double-stranded telomere repeats, and plays a protective role by preventing the ends of linear chromosomes being detected as double-strand breaks and inappropriately repaired (de Lange, 2018; Schmutz et al., 2017; Stansel et al., 2001; Van Ly et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to de Lange, 2018; Schmutz et al., 2017; Stansel et al., 2001; Van Ly et al., 2018.

claim: t-loops can be excised as telomere repeat-containing t-circles.
source: However, t-loops can be excised as telomere repeat-containing t-circles (Pickett et al., 2009; Pickett et al., 2011; Sarek et al., 2015; Tomaska et al., 2019) by the SLX1-4 complex, which is a structure-specific endonuclease (Fekairi, 2009; Vannier et al., 2012; Wan et al., 2013), and unregulated excision of t-loops results in critically short telomeres (Deng et al., 2013; Pickett et al., 2011; Rivera et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Pickett et al., 2009; Pickett et al., 2011; Sarek et al., 2015; Tomaska et al., 2019.

claim: t-loop excision is performed by the SLX1-4 complex, which is a structure-specific endonuclease.
source: However, t-loops can be excised as telomere repeat-containing t-circles (Pickett et al., 2009; Pickett et al., 2011; Sarek et al., 2015; Tomaska et al., 2019) by the SLX1-4 complex, which is a structure-specific endonuclease (Fekairi, 2009; Vannier et al., 2012; Wan et al., 2013), and unregulated excision of t-loops results in critically short telomeres (Deng et al., 2013; Pickett et al., 2011; Rivera et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Fekairi, 2009; Vannier et al., 2012; Wan et al., 2013.

claim: Unregulated excision of t-loops results in critically short telomeres.
source: However, t-loops can be excised as telomere repeat-containing t-circles (Pickett et al., 2009; Pickett et al., 2011; Sarek et al., 2015; Tomaska et al., 2019) by the SLX1-4 complex, which is a structure-specific endonuclease (Fekairi, 2009; Vannier et al., 2012; Wan et al., 2013), and unregulated excision of t-loops results in critically short telomeres (Deng et al., 2013; Pickett et al., 2011; Rivera et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Deng et al., 2013; Pickett et al., 2011; Rivera et al., 2017.

claim: The study exploited a hypervariable region of the HHV-6B genome to investigate the relationship between acquired and inherited virus.
source: We exploited a hypervariable region of the HHV-6B genome to investigate the relationship between acquired and inherited virus and revealed predominantly maternal transmission of acqHHV-6B in families.
evidence: The claim is based on the methods described in the study.

claim: The study revealed predominantly maternal transmission of acqHHV-6B in families.
source: We exploited a hypervariable region of the HHV-6B genome to investigate the relationship between acquired and inherited virus and revealed predominantly maternal transmission of acqHHV-6B in families.
evidence: The claim is based on data from the study.

claim: Some copies of acqHHV-6B in saliva from healthy adults gained a telomere, indicative of integration and latency.
source: Remarkably, we demonstrate that some copies of acqHHV-6B in saliva from healthy adults gained a telomere, indicative of integration and latency, and that the frequency of viral genome excision from telomeres in iciHHV-6B carriers is surprisingly high and varies between tissues.
evidence: The claim is based on data from the study.

claim: The frequency of viral genome excision from telomeres in iciHHV-6B carriers is surprisingly high and varies between tissues.
source: Remarkably, we demonstrate that some copies of acqHHV-6B in saliva from healthy adults gained a telomere, indicative of integration and latency, and that the frequency of viral genome excision from telomeres in iciHHV-6B carriers is surprisingly high and varies between tissues.
evidence: The claim is based on data from the study.

claim: Newly formed short telomeres generated by partial viral genome release are frequently lengthened, particularly in telomerase-expressing pluripotent cells.
source: In addition, newly formed short telomeres generated by partial viral genome release are frequently lengthened, particularly in telomerase-expressing pluripotent cells.
evidence: The claim is based on data from the study.

claim: iciHHV-6B carriers are mosaic for different iciHHV-6B structures, including circular extra-chromosomal forms that have the potential to reactivate.
source: Consequently, iciHHV-6B carriers are mosaic for different iciHHV-6B structures, including circular extra-chromosomal forms that have the potential to reactivate.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the data presented in the study.

claim: The study shows transmission of an HHV-6B strain from an iciHHV-6B mother to her non-iciHHV-6B son.
source: Finally, we show transmission of an HHV-6B strain from an iciHHV-6B mother to her non-iciHHV-6B son.
evidence: The claim is based on data from the study.

claim: iciHHV-6B can readily transition between telomere-integrated and free virus forms.
source: Altogether, we demonstrate that iciHHV-6B can readily transition between telomere-integrated and free virus forms.
evidence: The claim is based on data and inference from the study.

claim: A total of 102 DNA samples were analyzed: iciHHV-6B from 39 individuals (38.2%) and acqHHV-6B from 63 (61.8%) individuals.
source: A total of 102 DNA samples were analyzed: iciHHV-6B from 39 individuals (38.2%) and acqHHV-6B from 63 (61.8%) individuals (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The claim is based on data from the study.

claim: DRR-pvT1 can be divided into three regions from the DR421 primer (proximal, central, and distal), with most of the variation being due to differences in the number and distribution of telomere (TTAGGG) and degenerate telomere-like repeats in the proximal and central regions.
source: The analysis showed that DRR-pvT1 can be divided into three regions from the DR421 primer (proximal, central, and distal), with most of the variation being due to differences in the number and distribution of telomere (TTAGGG) and degenerate telomere-like repeats (predominantly CTATGG and CTAGGG) in the proximal and central regions.
evidence: The claim is based on data from the study.

claim: Among the 102 repeat patterns, 93 were different from each other, and 90 of these were detected in only a single donor or family.
source: Among the 102 repeat patterns, 93 were different from each other, and 90 of these were detected in only a single donor or family.
evidence: The claim is based on data from the study.

claim: The pvT1 repeat pattern was different in almost every unrelated individual with acqHHV-6B (61/63, 96.8%).
source: Remarkably, the pvT1 repeat pattern was different in almost every unrelated individual with acqHHV-6B (61/63, 96.8%) and also in the majority of iciHHV-6B individuals (30/39, 77.0%; 29/31, 93.5%, when the entire 9q iciHHV-6B group was excluded).
evidence: The claim is based on data from the study.

claim: The pvT1 repeat pattern was different in the majority of iciHHV-6B individuals (30/39, 77.0%; 29/31, 93.5%, when the entire 9q iciHHV-6B group was excluded).
source: Remarkably, the pvT1 repeat pattern was different in almost every unrelated individual with acqHHV-6B (61/63, 96.8%) and also in the majority of iciHHV-6B individuals (30/39, 77.0%; 29/31, 93.5%, when the entire 9q iciHHV-6B group was excluded).
evidence: The claim is based on data from the study.

claim: Saliva DNA was analyzed from 36 individuals in eight families (without iciHHV-6B) and DRR-pvT1 was successfully amplified and sequenced from 34 of them (94%).
source: Saliva DNA was analyzed from 36 individuals in eight families (without iciHHV-6B) and DRR-pvT1 was successfully amplified and sequenced from 34 of them (94%).
evidence: The claim is based on data from the study.

claim: 18 of the 20 children (90%) in these families had the same repeat pattern as one of their parents, presumably as a result of acqHHV-6B transmission directly from a parent or indirectly via a sibling.
source: 18 of the 20 children (90%) in these families had the same repeat pattern as one of their parents, presumably as a result of acqHHV-6B transmission directly from a parent (maternal transmission in six of the eight families and paternal transmission in one) or indirectly via a sibling (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is based on data from the study.

claim: Maternal transmission of acqHHV-6B occurred in six of the eight families and paternal transmission in one.
source: 18 of the 20 children (90%) in these families had the same repeat pattern as one of their parents, presumably as a result of acqHHV-6B transmission directly from a parent (maternal transmission in six of the eight families and paternal transmission in one) or indirectly via a sibling (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is based on data from the study.

claim: Analysis of DRR-pvT1 in the CEPH1375 family demonstrated the stability of the repeat patterns across three generations.
source: As a control, analysis of DRR-pvT1 repeat patterns in iciHHV-6B carriers in the CEPH1375 family demonstrated the stability of the repeat patterns across three generations (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is based on data from the study.

claim: All six individuals in the CEPH1375 family, shown previously to be iciHHV-6B carriers, shared an identical pattern, indicating that DRR-pvT1 in iciHHV-6B does not necessarily acquire mutations from one generation to the next.
source: All six individuals, shown previously to be iciHHV-6B carriers (Huang et al., 2014), shared an identical pattern, indicating that DRR-pvT1 in iciHHV-6B does not necessarily acquire mutations from one generation to the next.
evidence: The claim is based on data from the study.

claim: The study sequenced 10 iciHHV-6A and 5 iciHHV-6B genomes.
source: In total, 10 iciHHV-6A and 5 iciHHV-6B genomes were sequenced.
evidence: The claim is based on data from the study.

claim: The majority of iciHHV-6A genomes in European and North American carriers originate from three integration events at 17p, 18q, and 19q, with the time to the most recent common ancestor estimated at 23–105 thousand years ago.
source: These networks reinforce previous findings (Aswad et al., 2021; Greninger et al., 2018; Tweedy et al., 2016; Zhang et al., 2017), showing that the majority of iciHHV-6A genomes in European and North American carriers (including the 10 newly sequenced) originate from three integration events at 17p, 18q, and 19q, with the time to the most recent common ancestor estimated at 23–105 thousand years ago (Figure 2A, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: The claim is based on data from the study and citations to Aswad et al., 2021; Greninger et al., 2018; Tweedy et al., 2016; Zhang et al., 2017.

claim: iciHHV-6B carriers with European and North America ancestry originate from a larger number of integration events that occurred more recently (21–25 thousand years ago).
source: The networks also confirm that iciHHV-6B carriers with European and North America ancestry originate from a larger number of integration events that occurred more recently (21–25 thousand years ago; Supplementary file 2; Aswad et al., 2021; Greninger et al., 2018; Zhang et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is based on data from the study and citations to Aswad et al., 2021; Greninger et al., 2018; Zhang et al., 2017.

claim: Inclusion of the newly sequenced iciHHV-6B genomes added two new iciHHV-6B clades to the phylogenetic network, each defined by a distinct integration site.
source: Inclusion of the newly sequenced iciHHV-6B genomes added two new iciHHV-6B clades to the phylogenetic network, each defined by a distinct integration site (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is based on data from the study.

claim: Two potentially inactivating mutations, U14 in an iciHHV-6B clade and in U79 in an iciHHV-6A clade, must have arisen after integration.
source: Using the HHV-6 Explorer, we displayed two mutations that introduced stop codons in U79 in three of seven iciHHV-6A samples in the 17p clade and in U14 in one of three iciHHV-6B samples in the 17p (minor) clade (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), demonstrating that each mutation arose after integration.
evidence: The claim is based on data from the study.

claim: Individuals with 9q iciHHV-6B have a characteristic (CTATGG-TTAGTG-CTATGG) motif (pink-cyan-pink repeats) in the central region of DRR-pvT1.
source: For example, individuals with 9q iciHHV-6B have a characteristic (CTATGG-TTAGTG-CTATGG) motif (pink-cyan-pink repeats) in the central region of DRR-pvT1, as well as a rare (TTAGAG) repeat (peach) that is found infrequently outside this group.
evidence: The claim is based on data from the study.

claim: Viral sequences assigned to the 17p (major) iciHHV-6B group had similar DRR-pvT1 repeat patterns with a characteristic (GTAGTG) (blue) repeat at the fifth position.
source: Also, viral sequences assigned to the 17p (major) iciHHV-6B group by genome sequence identity and shared 17p subtelomere-iciHHV-6B junction sequences (HGDP01065, DER512, 801018, and ORCA1622) (Zhang et al., 2017) had similar DRR-pvT1 repeat patterns with a characteristic (GTAGTG) (blue) repeat at the fifth position, replacing the (TTAGTG) (cyan) repeat seen in almost all other pvT1 repeat patterns (Figure 3A, Figure 1—figure supplement 1, Supplementary file 3).
evidence: The claim is based on data from the study.

claim: DRR-pvT1 analysis can be used effectively to discriminate between HHV-6B strains circulating in communities (61/63 different DRR-pvT1 sequences in saliva from healthy non-iciHHV-6B donors in the UK).
source: We showed that DRR-pvT1 repeat patterns can be used effectively to discriminate between HHV-6B strains circulating in communities (61/63 different DRR-pvT1 sequences in saliva from healthy non-iciHHV-6B donors in the UK).
evidence: The claim is based on data from the study.

claim: Low-level HHV-6B was detected in 44 samples (84.6%) with a mean value of 0.00145 copies per cell (range 0.0000233–0.0125).
source: Using this sensitive approach, low-level HHV-6B was detected in 44 samples (84.6%) with a mean value of 0.00145 copies per cell (range 0.0000233–0.0125).
evidence: The claim is based on data from the study.

claim: Two kidney DNA samples, K1 and K10, were also positive for HHV-6B at 0.000525 and 0.0124 copies per cell, respectively.
source: Two kidney DNA samples, K1 and K10, were also positive for HHV-6B at 0.000525 and 0.0124 copies per cell, respectively (Figure 4A and D).
evidence: The claim is based on data from the study.

claim: An average of 0.95% (range 0–1.98%) of HHV-6B genomes resulted in pvT1 amplification, indicative of telomeric integration.
source: For the eight samples analyzed, an average of 0.95% (range 0–1.98%) of HHV-6B genomes resulted in pvT1 amplification, indicative of telomeric integration.
evidence: The claim is based on data from the study.

claim: The ratio of DR:PAC1 in an iciHHV-6B sample (4B-11p15.5) was approximately 2:1.
source: As expected, the ratio of DR:PAC1 in an iciHHV-6B sample (4B-11p15.5) was approximately 2:1, whereas the ratio in acqHHV6-B samples in saliva samples was approximately 2:2 (Figure 4E).
evidence: The claim is based on data from the study.

claim: The ratio of DR:PAC1 in acqHHV6-B samples in saliva samples was approximately 2:2.
source: As expected, the ratio of DR:PAC1 in an iciHHV-6B sample (4B-11p15.5) was approximately 2:1, whereas the ratio in acqHHV6-B samples in saliva samples was approximately 2:2 (Figure 4E).
evidence: The claim is based on data from the study.

claim: Most acqHHV-6B genomes in saliva samples are not integrated.
source: This shows that most acqHHV-6B genomes in saliva samples are not integrated, consistent with the STELA data that revealed only low-level telomeric integration of acqHHV-6B genomes in saliva DNA samples.
evidence: The claim is based on data from the study.

claim: The average frequency of DRL-T2 truncations with novel telomere formation was 1 in 120 cells.
source: The average frequency of DRL-T2 truncations with novel telomere formation was 1 in 120 cells, but there were significant differences between DNAs from different cell types.
evidence: The claim is based on data from the study.

claim: The number of truncations per cell was lowest in blood and saliva DNA, with an average of 1 in 300 (0.0033 per cell) and 1 in 320 (0.0031), respectively.
source: The number of truncations per cell was lowest in blood and saliva DNA, with an average of 1 in 300 (0.0033 per cell) and 1 in 320 (0.0031), respectively, and approximately double this in sperm at 1 in 160 cells (0.00627 per cell).
evidence: The claim is based on data from the study.

claim: An astonishingly high number of DRL-T2 truncations were observed in LCLs (0.015 per cell) and pluripotent cells (0.014 per cell), equating to approximately 1 in every 70 cells.
source: An astonishingly high number of DRL-T2 truncations were observed in LCLs (0.015 per cell) and pluripotent cells (0.014 per cell), equating to approximately 1 in every 70 cells.
evidence: The claim is based on data from the study.

claim: Released circular DR molecules were detected using an inverse PCR approach.
source: Furthermore, released circular DR molecules were detected using an inverse PCR approach (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is based on data from the study.

claim: The frequency of truncation events at DRL-T2 increased significantly from 0.0162 to 0.0290 per cell at the highest TSA concentration.
source: The frequency of truncation events at DRL-T2 increased significantly from 0.0162 to 0.0290 per cell at the highest TSA concentration.
evidence: The claim is based on data from the study.

claim: iciHHV-6B chromatin conformation influences the chance of t-loop formation at the telomere-like repeats within the viral genome and subsequent excision events.
source: This suggests that iciHHV-6B chromatin conformation influences the chance of t-loop formation at the telomere-like repeats within the viral genome and subsequent excision events.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the data presented in the study.

claim: Six of the lengthened amplicons from three DNA samples (4B-11p15.5, d56, and NWA008) comprised the expected flanking sequence followed by a uniform array of (TTAGGG) repeats exceeding the known length of DRL-T2 for the sample, thus showing that some of the novel telomeres formed at DRL-T2 had been lengthened.
source: To address this, six of the lengthened amplicons from three DNA samples (4B-11p15.5, d56, and NWA008) were sequenced. All comprised the expected flanking sequence followed by a uniform array of (TTAGGG) repeats exceeding the known length of DRL-T2 for the sample, thus showing that some of the novel telomeres formed at DRL-T2 had been lengthened (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is based on data from the study.

claim: Telomerase activity was detected at a low level in the 4B-11p15.5 and other iciHHV-6B LCLs.
source: Telomerase activity was detected at a low level in the 4B-11p15.5 and other iciHHV-6B LCLs (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C), consistent with a telomerase-mediated lengthening of newly formed telomeres.
evidence: The claim is based on data from the study.

claim: The proportion of lengthened telomeres was higher in the pluripotent cell lines, blood DNA, and saliva samples, and lower in the LCLs and sperm samples.
source: The proportion of lengthened telomeres was higher in the pluripotent cell lines, blood DNA, and saliva samples, and lower in the LCLs and sperm samples (Supplementary file 5).
evidence: The claim is based on data from the study.

claim: Differences between DRR-pvT1 and DRL-pvT1 within a single iciHHV-6B genome were found in many of the iciHHV-6B samples analyzed (24/35, 68.6%).
source: Differences between DRR-pvT1 and DRL-pvT1 within a single iciHHV-6B genome were found in many of the iciHHV-6B samples analyzed (24/35, 68.6%; Figure 6A, Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is based on data from the study.

claim: Truncations at DRR-T1 were detected in all 10 iciHHV-6B samples with larger pvT1 size differences.
source: Consequently, 10 iciHHV-6B samples, with larger pvT1 size differences, were selected and truncations at DRR-T1 were detected in all.
evidence: The claim is based on data from the study.

claim: The frequency of newly formed telomeres at DRR-T1 varied between samples (0.0002–0.0029 per cell).
source: In summary, the frequency of newly formed telomeres at DRR-T1 varied between samples (0.0002–0.0029 per cell; Figure 6C, Supplementary file 6).
evidence: The claim is based on data from the study.

claim: Three individuals carry iciHHV-6B DR-only (308006 and SAL018 in the present study, and KEN071).
source: To date, we have identified three individuals who carry iciHHV-6B DR-only (308006 and SAL018 in the present study, and KEN071 Huang et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is based on data from the study.

claim: The DR-only iciHHV-6B in SAL018 and KEN071 share the common 17p (major) subtelomere-iciHHV-6B junction that is also found in 801018, d44, and others.
source: Using this approach, we found that the DR-only iciHHV-6B in SAL018 and KEN071 share the common 17p (major) subtelomere-iciHHV-6B junction that is also found in 801018, d44, and others (Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is based on data from the study.

claim: The pattern of telomere and degenerate repeats across a subtelomere-iciHHV-6B junction in the DR-only iciHHV-6B sample 308006 closely matched those in full-length iciHHV-6B individuals 401027 and 410005.
source: Similarly, the pattern of telomere and degenerate repeats across a subtelomere-iciHHV-6B junction (amplified by subtelomere primer 2p2) in the DR-only iciHHV-6B sample 308006 closely matched those in full-length iciHHV-6B individuals 401027 and 410005 (Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is based on data from the study.

claim: The DR-only status has arisen independently, on at least two occasions, by loss of U and one copy of DR in the germline of an ancestor with a full-length iciHHV-6B genome.
source: The existence of shared integration sites for the full-length and DR-only iciHHV-6B carriers at two different chromosome ends clearly establishes that the DR-only status has arisen independently, on at least two occasions, by loss of U and one copy of DR in the germline of an ancestor with a full-length iciHHV-6B genome.
evidence: The claim is based on data and inference from the study.

claim: In family Rx-F6a, the mother (G3P1) had a low acqHHV-6B load in saliva (0.00035 copies per cell), but both her children were iciHHV-6B carriers.
source: In one family (Rx-F6a), the mother (G3P1) had a low acqHHV-6B load in saliva (0.00035 copies per cell), but both her children were iciHHV-6B carriers.
evidence: The claim is based on data from the study.

claim: The DRR-pvT1 repeat patterns in the children in family Rx-F6a were identical and presumed to have been inherited from the father.
source: The DRR-pvT1 repeat patterns in the children were identical and presumed to have been inherited from the father, who was not available for testing.
evidence: The claim is based on data and inference from the study.

claim: In family Rx-F3a, the mother (G3P2) was an iciHHV-6B carrier and her daughter (G4P3) had approximately two copies of iciHHV-6B per cell.
source: Quantification of HHV-6B in saliva samples from another family (Rx-F3a, Figure 7B) showed that the mother (G3P2) was an iciHHV-6B carrier and that her daughter (G4P3) had approximately two copies of iciHHV-6B per cell.
evidence: The claim is based on data from the study.

claim: Identical DRR-pvT1 repeat patterns between the mother and daughter in family Rx-F3a proved maternal inheritance of one iciHHV-6B copy.
source: Identical DRR-pvT1 repeat patterns between the mother and daughter proved maternal inheritance of one iciHHV-6B copy.
evidence: The claim is based on data from the study.

claim: The son (G4P1) in family Rx-F3a had 0.00025 copies of HHV-6B per cell in saliva DNA, consistent with the level expected from acqHHV-6B infection.
source: The son (G4P1) had 0.00025 copies of HHV-6B per cell in saliva DNA, consistent with the level expected from acqHHV-6B infection (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is based on data from the study.

claim: The DRR-pvT1 repeat pattern in the son (G4P1) in family Rx-F3a was identical to that in the mother and one copy of iciHHV-6B in his sister.
source: Importantly, the DRR-pvT1 repeat pattern in the son (G4P1) was identical to that in the mother and one copy of iciHHV-6B in his sister.
evidence: The claim is based on data from the study.

claim: The DRR-pvT1 repeat pattern in the son (G4P1) in family Rx-F3a was not seen outside this family among 102 DRR-pvT1 repeat patterns.
source: This repeat pattern was not seen outside this family among 102 DRR-pvT1 repeat patterns (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is based on data from the study.

claim: iciHHV-6B genome excision occurred in the mother in family Rx-F3a and the reactivated HHV-6B was then transmitted to the non-iciHHV-6B son.
source: These observations strongly suggest that iciHHV-6B genome excision occurred in the mother and that the reactivated HHV-6B was then transmitted to the non-iciHHV-6B son, who retained residual viral sequences in his saliva.
evidence: The claim is based on data and inference from the study.

claim: The study demonstrates that some copies of acqHHV-6B in saliva acquire a telomere, indicative of integration in somatic cells in vivo.
source: We demonstrated that some copies of HHV-6B in saliva acquire a telomere, indicative of integration in somatic cells in vivo and as previously detected in vitro (Arbuckle et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is based on data from the study.

claim: The viral load in the saliva samples was low, and the number of HHV-6B genomes with a telomere was small.
source: The viral load in the saliva samples was low, as seen in some other studies (Leibovitch et al., 2014; Leibovitch et al., 2019; Turriziani et al., 2014), and the number of HHV-6B genomes with a telomere was small (Figure 4, Supplementary file 4), which is consistent with the majority of HHV-6B genomes present as viral particles in saliva (Jarrett et al., 1990).
evidence: The claim is based on data from the study and citations to Leibovitch et al., 2014; Leibovitch et al., 2019; Turriziani et al., 2014; Jarrett et al., 1990.

claim: The frequencies of iciHHV-6B truncations at DRL-T2 (range, 0.014–0.0031 per cell) and DRR-T1 (range, 0.0002–0.0029 per cell) are surprisingly high in vivo.
source: The frequencies of iciHHV-6B truncations at DRL-T2 (range, 0.014–0.0031 per cell) and DRR-T1 (range, 0.0002–0.0029 per cell) are not directly comparable because they were ascertained by different approaches that have different efficiencies, but both are surprisingly high in vivo (Figures 5 and 6).
evidence: The claim is based on data from the study.

claim: Tissues in iciHHV-6B carriers must be mosaic for different compositions of the iciHHV-6B genome.
source: This demonstrates that tissues in iciHHV-6B carriers must be mosaic for different compositions of the iciHHV-6B genome.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the data presented in the study.

claim: A high percentage of newly formed telomeres at DRL-T2 were lengthened.
source: It is therefore remarkable that a high percentage of newly formed telomeres at DRL-T2 were lengthened.
evidence: The claim is based on data from the study.

claim: The frequency of DRL-T2 telomere lengthening was highest in circulating white blood cells and in two pluripotent cell lines.
source: The frequency of DRL-T2 telomere lengthening was highest in circulating white blood cells and in two pluripotent cell lines (Figure 5) consistent with lengthening by telomerase.
evidence: The claim is based on data from the study.

claim: iciHHV-6A/6B genomes are more likely to be excised and reactivated in undifferentiated or pluripotent cells.
source: From these observations and the increase in viral genome excision events in TSA-treated cells, we also propose that iciHHV-6A/6B genomes are more likely to be excised and reactivated in undifferentiated or pluripotent cells.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the data presented in the study.

claim: The potential for iciHHV-6A/6B genome excision, viral gene expression, or full reactivation has the potential to be deleterious during early development.
source: By extrapolation, the potential for iciHHV-6A/6B genome excision, viral gene expression, or full reactivation has the potential to be deleterious during early development (Miura et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is based on speculation and a citation to Miura et al., 2020.

claim: The study identified individuals with full-length iciHHV-6B or DR-only genomes that fall into the same clade in the phylogenetic tree.
source: First, we identified individuals with full-length iciHHV-6B or DR-only genomes that fall into the same clade in the phylogenetic tree (Figure 3).
evidence: The claim is based on data from the study.

claim: The different iciHHV-6B structures (full-length and DR-only) are carried in the same telomere-allele at the particular chromosome end.
source: This demonstrates that the different iciHHV-6B structures are carried in the same telomere-allele at the particular chromosome end, and it proves that these DR-only carriers have arisen by germline excision of U-DR in an ancestor.
evidence: The claim is based on data and inference from the study.

claim: DR-only carriers have arisen by germline excision of U-DR in an ancestor.
source: This demonstrates that the different iciHHV-6B structures are carried in the same telomere-allele at the particular chromosome end, and it proves that these DR-only carriers have arisen by germline excision of U-DR in an ancestor.
evidence: The claim is based on data and inference from the study.

claim: The fact that DR-only status has occurred independently at least twice suggests that this is a relatively common event.
source: The fact that this has occurred independently at least twice suggests that this is a relatively common event, and this is supported by our evidence that new telomere formation at DRR-T1 occurs at a measurable frequency in sperm DNA.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the data presented in the study.

claim: The study shows an example of probable reactivation of iciHHV-6B in a mother with transmission to her son, who carries a very low load of acqHHV-6B with the same distinctive DRR-pvT1 repeat pattern in his saliva.
source: Second, we show an example of probable reactivation of iciHHV-6B in a mother with transmission to her son, who carries a very low load of acqHHV-6B with the same distinctive DRR-pvT1 repeat pattern in his saliva.
evidence: The claim is based on data from the study.

claim: The BIOSTAT-CHF cohort screening identified 19 iciHHV-6A/6B-positive samples (9 iciHHV-6A, 0.36%, and 10 iciHHV-6B, 0.40%, one of which was iciHHV-6B DR-only).
source: This identified 19 iciHHV-6A/6B-positive samples (9 iciHHV-6A, 0.36%, and 10 iciHHV-6B, 0.40%, one of which was iciHHV-6B DR-only).
evidence: The claim is based on data from the study.

claim: Five iciHHV-6B carriers were identified among the saliva donors: three with a single copy of iciHHV-6B, one with two copies of iciHHV-6B, and one with iciHHV-6B DR-only.
source: Five iciHHV-6B carriers were identified among the saliva donors: three with a single copy of iciHHV-6B, one with two copies of iciHHV-6B, and one with iciHHV-6B DR-only.
evidence: The claim is based on data from the study.

claim: No STELA products were generated from HT1080 among 900 STELA reactions, total 4.5 μg DNA screened.
source: No STELA products were generated from HT1080 among 900 STELA reactions, total 4.5 μg DNA screened.
evidence: The claim is based on data from the study.
